issues.description: StockIngredient constructor signature is inconsistent across artifacts. The problem statement UML and the reference solution define StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity), but the template defines StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity, boolean strictValidation). Students following the UML/spec cannot instantiate StockIngredient as required without changing the template API, and implementing SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery as specified will not compile against the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML/spec by adding a 3-argument constructor StockIngredient(String name, int price, int quantity). If the strictValidation behavior should remain, keep the 4-arg constructor as optional and delegate from the 3-arg constructor (or remove the boolean parameter entirely).

issues.description: Stock exposes a public method setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) in both template and solution, but this method is not part of the public API described in the problem statement UML (which lists only add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, emptyStock). This creates an API mismatch and may lead students to rely on an undocumented method instead of the intended stock-management methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) update the problem statement UML/spec to explicitly include setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) as a provided helper, or (b) remove it from the template public API (or make it non-public and avoid using it in starter code like Main) to keep the exposed API consistent with the UML.
